messages:
Elaine: FYI support flagged sudden p95/p99 spike for /v1/generate in us-west-2 starting ~11:22 UTC. A handful of customers reporting timeouts and slow responses.
Sam: any recent rollouts or config changes around 11:15-11:25?
Elaine: there was a batching tuning rollout at 11:18 (increased batch_window_ms and max_batch_tokens for rdx-hf-large). Canary looked ok but full rollout hit ~11:21.
Tariq: posting quick logs from telemetry cluster (trimmed):
[11:22:09] node-a latency=42ms p95=610ms p99=1250ms queue_ms=410ms batching_ms=320ms kv_hit=false
[11:23:02] node-d latency=58ms p95=720ms p99=1800ms queue_ms=900ms batching_ms=380ms kv_hit=false
Matt: queue_ms and batching_ms are the smoking gun: requests are piling into bigger batches -> head-of-line stalls.
Sam: immediate plan: 1) pause rollout 2) revert batching_window to previous value 3) enable emergency fallback routing to rdx-medium for non-enterprise traffic 4) apply temporary soft rate-limit header to clients (X-RateLimit-Warn)
Elaine: pause applied at 11:24. Kicking a revert now to batch_window=15ms and max_batch_tokens back to 1024. Canary at 11:26.
Jess: ops-bot, set circuit-breaker for rdx-hf-large in us-west-2 to OPENING when p99>900ms for 2m and auto-route to fallback model after 3 triggers.
ops-bot: circuit-breaker rule created: trigger window=2m, threshold p99>900ms, action=route-to-fallback (rdx-medium), cooldown=5m.
Tariq: also lowering max_concurrent_sequences on the large pool by 30% to limit head-of-line blocking. Doing that now.
Sam: while revert runs, enable a regional fallback policy: for us-west-2 route up to 40% of traffic to rdx-medium for hosted customers without SLA tag. Use gradual ramp if p95 doesn't improve.
Matt: added an alert: "batching_ms_delta" when batching_ms increases by >200ms over baseline within 5m and include node id list + avg queue_ms in payload.
Elaine: canary 11:29 health: p95 ~70ms, p99 ~190ms on canary nodes. Revert rolling to 100% now.
Jess: sending support update to affected customers: "We identified increased tail latency caused by a batching config change and have reverted the change. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause and mitigations." :email:
Sam: follow-ups to harden rollout: - add a pre-rollout SLO gate: fail rollout if canary p99 delta >25% relative to baseline for 10m - add automatic batch-size increases only when canary latency and queue_ms are within thresholds - add automatic fallback-by-region if queue_ms>250ms for 2m - expose an emergency throttling API to Support to quickly cap new sessions
Tariq: long-term: add synthetic KV-cache-aware load tests in the rollout pipeline (simulate cold-KV runs + variable seq lengths) and test impact of batching changes on p99.
Matt: also propose a graceful degrade route: when p99 spikes, prefer routing by model-size then by region - e.g., try rdx-medium in same region before cross-region failover to avoid cold caches.
Elaine: creating incident postmortem and playbook entry: include exact rollback commands, ops-bot circuit-breaker rule template, support message template, and the throttling header behavior.
ops-bot: incident marked RESOLVED at 11:40:20 by Elaine. Summary: batching_window increase caused queueing and tail-latency; mitigations: paused rollout, reverted config, regional model fallback, temporary concurrency cap and soft-rate warnings. Action items: add rollout SLO guardrail, add batching_ms alert, add KV-aware synthetic test, document throttling playbook.
Jess: filing customer follow-ups and tagging tickets. Scheduling 30m retro to validate rollback automation and runbook clarity.
Sam: nice work all. After postmortem, let's add an automated abort-on-p99-regression step in the rollout pipeline and a circuit-breaker template for all model pools. :thumbsup:
